title.en: JANUS Connection Scan — Invariant Survival and Source-Level Residual Structure
title.ru: JANUS Connection Scan — выживание инварианта и остаточная структура исходных данных

scan_scope: selected proof, causal-topology, authority and provenance records

primary_hidden_node_candidate.name: SOURCE_LEVEL_RESIDUAL
primary_hidden_node_candidate.definition: The portion of an apparent connection that remains after removing prior JANUS interpretations, historical lineage, authority labels, canonical relational vocabulary, source ordering, and detector-specific features.
primary_hidden_node_candidate.core_question: What, if anything, remains connected when the machine is prevented from using the evidence-production environment that originally made the connection visible?
primary_hidden_node_candidate.why_seventh_order: This is above the recursive-memory and epistemic-covariance layers: the target is the residual relationship that survives removal of those layers rather than another cause within them.

emergent_invariants.name: RESIDUAL_STRUCTURE_IS_THE_RELEVANT_OBJECT
emergent_invariants.description: For a Connection system, the most informative candidate may be the part of a relationship that survives removal of memory, provenance, authority, ontology, ordering and detector-specific context.

emergent_invariants.name: DEPENDENCY_WEIGHTED_CONNECTION
emergent_invariants.description: Connection strength should be decomposed into raw detection strength and the fraction attributable to shared upstream dependencies.

emergent_invariants.name: CROSS_REPRESENTATION_STABILITY
emergent_invariants.description: A relationship that appears under materially different representations is less likely to be caused solely by one canonical vocabulary or detector feature family.

emergent_invariants.name: ORDER_INVARIANCE_AS_CONTROL
emergent_invariants.description: If candidate relationships depend strongly on traversal order, archive layout, or chronology of prior discoveries, order may be acting as a hidden state variable.

emergent_invariants.name: EXTERNALITY_REQUIREMENT_FOR_STRONG_SUPPORT
emergent_invariants.description: Survival inside the Meta Registry is still internal evidence; stronger support requires replication using source material or observers outside the same evidence-production environment.

connections.machine_observation: The registry's own methodology increasingly treats prior scans, authority metadata and relational ontology as dependencies to remove. This implies that the target object of high-value Connection discovery is the residual structure that remains after those dependencies are removed.
connections.pattern_description: The Connection project has recursively transformed from finding repeated relations to asking which relation survives the destruction of the machinery that made the relation salient.
connections.why_non_obvious: Most pattern systems optimize detection before dependency removal. Here the dependency-removal result becomes the primary object of interest.
alternative_explanations: This may simply be methodological caution rather than a distinct source-level structure.
Aggressive ablation can remove genuinely informative context and produce false negatives.
connections.falsification_route: Implement the full context-removal battery and determine whether any candidate connections remain stable while an independent detector agrees on the same residual edge.

connections.machine_observation: Raw recurrence counts currently do not distinguish independent recurrence from recurrence generated by shared scans, vocabulary, provenance or source-pipeline membership.
connections.pattern_description: Two connections with the same raw recurrence count may carry very different evidentiary value if one is repeated across independent source families and the other is repeated only inside the same research lineage.
connections.why_non_obvious: Counting edges is easy; assigning dependency structure to those edges is harder and changes the meaning of recurrence.
alternative_explanations: Source dependence may already be encoded sufficiently by provenance fields.
A numerical dependency penalty could falsely downgrade genuine related records that naturally share infrastructure.
connections.falsification_route: Construct a provenance dependency graph and compare raw edge counts with dependency-collapsed edge counts on a repository-preserving null corpus.

source_objects: selected raw source objects from data/proofs/ and registry/causal_topology/
connections.machine_observation: The strongest proposed relations are currently defined using a common relational vocabulary. A materially independent representation is required to determine whether the relation exists outside that vocabulary.
connections.pattern_description: A stable edge across multiple representations is qualitatively different from a repeated label inside a single representation space.
connections.why_non_obvious: Repeated labels can look like repeated mechanisms even when they result from the same compression scheme.
alternative_explanations: The canonical vocabulary may be a faithful abstraction of a real structural invariant.
Independent representations may be correlated because they are all derived from the same raw text.
connections.falsification_route: Blindly encode raw source objects using an independently designed feature space and test whether the same candidate edges emerge without JANUS relation labels.

connections.machine_observation: The registry preserves chronology and a navigation order, while previous scans explicitly use prior scans as context. This creates a plausible dependence on sequence position.
connections.pattern_description: A relation that appears only after a particular sequence of scans may be partly generated by accumulated context rather than by the raw source set.
connections.why_non_obvious: Git history makes sequence look like provenance only; for a recursive detector, sequence can also be an active input.
alternative_explanations: Chronology may legitimately expose temporal relations that should not be shuffled away.
Order tests must distinguish temporal signal from detector path dependence.
connections.falsification_route: Run source-order permutations while preserving timestamps as explicit metadata; compare stable temporal connections with order-dependent artifacts.

connections.machine_observation: The Meta Registry already distinguishes internal evidence from independent replication and treats historical authority as distinct from current external authority.
connections.pattern_description: The same epistemic boundary that protects AIFC and other technical claims should apply to Connection itself: a relation found repeatedly inside one curated repository remains an internal hypothesis until an independent source environment reproduces it.
connections.why_non_obvious: Connection is a meta-analysis layer, so it can easily mistake breadth of internal coverage for breadth of independent evidence.
alternative_explanations: Some Connection questions are intentionally archival and do not require external replication.
External replication can be inappropriate for purely historical or symbolic relations.
connections.falsification_route: Classify each candidate by whether external replication is applicable, then require outside-source confirmation only for candidates whose claim depends on source independence.

seventh_order_graph.candidate_hidden_path: RAW_SOURCE -> remove {PRIOR_INTERPRETATIONS, PROVENANCE, AUTHORITY, ONTOLOGY, ORDER, DETECTOR_BIAS} -> RESIDUAL_STRUCTURE -> EXTERNAL_REPLICATION
seventh_order_graph.critical_prediction: The highest-value candidate connections should retain a non-trivial residual edge after context and detector dependency removal.
seventh_order_graph.counter_prediction: If nearly all strong connections collapse under dependency removal, the previous Connection density was primarily epistemic covariance rather than source-level structure.

next_scan_strategy.name: RESIDUAL_EDGE_BENCHMARK
next_scan_strategy.target: Measure which connections survive systematic removal of the Meta Registry's own memory, vocabulary, selection, authority and ordering effects.
tests: RAW_ONLY: expose raw source content and minimal immutable IDs only.
MEMORY_BLIND: exclude all previous Connection scans and derived interpretations.
AUTHORITY_BLIND: exclude evidence classes, current-authority labels and risk classes.
LINEAGE_BLIND: anonymize author, repository path, historical naming and chronology where temporal information is not part of the claim.
ONTOLOGY_SWAP: use an independently designed representation.
ORDER_SHUFFLE: randomize traversal order while preserving explicit event timestamps where causally relevant.
REPOSITORY_NULL: preserve graph degree, metadata shape, file sizes and schema but destroy semantic relations.
EXTERNAL_REPLICATION: reproduce the strongest surviving relation with source material outside JANUS Meta Registry.
next_scan_strategy.promotion_rule: A connection may gain evidentiary status only after surviving a predefined covariance-breaking battery appropriate to its claim class. Survival is not proof of causation or novelty.

limitations: The scan identifies a methodological target and structural hypotheses; it does not report the results of the proposed ablation experiments.
The current repository alone cannot establish external replication or global novelty.
Removing context can create false negatives, so ablation must be interpreted as a robustness test rather than as a truth oracle.
canonical_rule: JANUS should trust a connection more only when the connection survives removal of the machinery that made it easy to see.
